(a) Emergency Designation.—This title is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 4(g) of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010 (2 U.S.C. 933(g)). 
    (b) Designation in Senate.—In the Senate, this title is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 403(a) 
of S. Con. Res. 13 (111th Congress), the concurrent resolution on the budget for fiscal year 2010.

fable.w: This section only designates the title as an emergency requirement for budget-enforcement purposes under PAYGO and a Senate concurrent budget resolution. The tempting reading is that a "designation in Senate" is a procedural step, but it stays entirely inside Congress and the federal budget process. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: This title is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 4(g) of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010

opus.w: This section only labels the title as an emergency requirement for budget-scoring purposes under PAYGO and a Senate budget resolution. It does not involve any party outside the federal government: there is no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue. The mention of the Senate and a concurrent resolution might look procedural, but Congress is inside the federal government.
opus.s: This title is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 4(g) of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010 (2 U.S.C. 933(g)).

qwen_chat.w: This section simply designates the title as an emergency requirement for budgetary purposes under the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act and Senate budget resolutions. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public). The mention of the Senate refers to an internal legislative designation, not public participation.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Emergency Designation.—This title is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 4(g) of the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010 (2 U.S.C. 933(g)).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that because the text mentions the Senate and a concurrent resolution, it involves legislative participation or consultation. However, this section merely designates the title as an "emergency requirement" for budgetary scoring purposes under specific acts. It does not require the federal government to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or coordinate with states/tribes before making a decision. It is an internal procedural designation within the legislative and executive budget process.
